picks.title: More Than Half of Teachers Lack Training to Teach English Learners, Survey Finds
picks.take: An EdWeek Research Center survey of 930 teachers found 58 percent got little or no EL training in their teacher prep, and about 55 percent get little from district PD. Small districts under 2,500 students fare worst at 67 percent. That describes most of Mississippi, where the content teacher is usually the EL program.
picks.try: Pick one language move you already use, such as a sentence frame, and ask your EL specialist to watch one class period and tune it.

picks.title: Getting to Know Your ELLs' Literacy Background
picks.take: Colorín Colorado's updated guide walks through finding out whether a student reads in the home language before planning literacy support: check the home-language survey, have the student read a short passage aloud, look at ELPT data, and ask the family. One example student's Spanish literacy went unnoticed for over a year.
picks.try: Hand a newcomer a short passage in the home language and listen for a minute; a fluent reader needs transfer work, not phonics from scratch.

picks.title: After Layoffs and Cuts, Ed. Dept. Funds New English Learner Teacher Grants
picks.take: The Education Department awarded about $50 million to 12 National Professional Development grantees after cutting 28 grants last year. Winners needed a state endorsement letter and mostly fund ESL endorsements for general-education teachers, as in Wyoming and South Dakota. No Mississippi project is named, so local training still depends on district and MDE money.
picks.try: Ask your principal whether the district has a path to an ESL endorsement for content teachers, and who pays for it.
